The error numbers, and telling a raw result from an error.

<h2 id="eperm"><code>EPERM</code></h2>

```rux
pub const EPERM: int64 = 1;
```

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Linux/Src/Errors.rux#L15)

<h2 id="maximum-errno"><code>MaximumErrno</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MaximumErrno: int64 = 4095;
```

The largest error number the kernel's reserved range holds.
A raw result below `-MaximumErrno` is a value, not an error.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Linux/Src/Errors.rux#L152)

<h2 id="is-error"><code>IsError</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsError(result: int64) -> bool
```

Whether a raw system-call result is one of the kernel's reserved error values.
`result` is read by value. True for `-4095` through `-1`, and false for everything else, including every valid
mapping address a memory call returns.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Linux/Src/Errors.rux#L161)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type    | Description            |
| -------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `result` | `int64` | the raw result to test |

**Returns**: whether it is one of the reserved error values

<h2 id="errno"><code>Errno</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Errno(result: int64) -> int64
```

The error number a raw system-call result carries, or zero when it carries none.
`result` is read by value; the number is returned by copy, positive, as a man page names it. A successful result
gives zero, which is not an error number and never collides with one.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Linux/Src/Errors.rux#L172)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type    | Description            |
| -------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `result` | `int64` | the raw result to read |

**Returns**: the error number, positive, or zero when the result carries none
